title: Quantum physics seems strange because intuition trusts every nearby counterfactual

statements.text: Human intuition takes every counterfactual world that closely resembles the real one, by a Euclidean measure, to be possible. On the invariant set this is false, and the apparent strangeness of quantum physics comes from failing to tell realistic counterfactual states from unrealistic ones.

sources.quote: the reason we find quantum physics so difficult to understand is because our intuition, that all counterfactual worlds which sufficiently well resemble the real world are plausible worlds, is false
